chunks: And whatever is in it from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni - may Allah have mercy on him - I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Asam Al-Kulayni, and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-Sanani - may Allah be pleased with them - from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni; and likewise all of the book Al-Kafi, I have narrated it from them from him through his transmitters.

key_terms.السَّنَانِيِّ: Al-Sanani (referring to Muhammad ibn Ahmad, a known transmitter)
key_terms.الْكَافِي: Al-Kafi (the primary hadith book of Shia Islam)
key_terms.الْكُلَيْنِيِّ: Al-Kulayni (referring to Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, the author of Al-Kafi)
key_terms.رِجَالِهِ: his transmitters/men (referring to the chain of narrators)

ai.seo_question: Who are the transmitters of Al-Kulayni's Al-Kafi according to this chain?
ai.summary: This passage provides a crucial isnad (transmission chain of transmission) linking Shaykh al-Saduq directly to the primary compiler of Al-Kafi, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub Al-Kulayni, thereby validating the authenticity of the text within Shia hadith scholarship. By citing three distinct intermediaries—Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Asam, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-Sanani—the author demonstrates the rigorous verification process (tahqiq) characteristic of the classical period, ensuring the reliability of the narrations for legal and theological derivation.
